papers.summary: Spectral weight decay uses additive singular-value shrinkage. In 124M–500M LLaMA experiments, it reports better SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss and improved clean-test accuracy under label noise.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, low-rank compressibility, and memorization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon’s geometry to favor structured channel pruning. On a 1B LLaMA-style model, it preserves its own perplexity through 80% pruning, but its unpruned perplexity is worse than Muon’s, 12.84 versus 10.92.
papers.relevance: A direct test of the trade-off between training quality and learned compressibility.

evidence.quote: Overall, BMuon trades some unpruned quality for substantially greater robustness to structured channel pruning.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon combines structured weights with matrix-aware optimization. At a 6.89B dense reference size, its measured peak memory is 52.94 GB versus 68.87 GB for dense Muon, and full-step time is 1638.6 versus 2986.9 ms.
papers.relevance: Connects LLM pretraining quality, memory, and wall-clock cost across model sizes.

evidence.quote: The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Clean approximates SOAP preconditioners with Nyström sketching; Q-Clean compresses optimizer states further. At LLaMA-1.3B, the reported optimizer-state memory is 4.48 GB for Clean and 1.28 GB for Q-Clean, versus 5.11 GB for AdamW.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses low-rank optimizer-state compression and the quality–memory–time trade-off in pretraining.

evidence.quote: Clean reaches AdamW’s final performance in 64 hours instead of 81, while simultaneously reducing the optimizer memory footprint.

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting gradient subspaces using streaming $k$-PCA. In a 130M pretraining example at rank 16, it reports validation perplexity of 43.61 versus 60.29 for GaLore and 54.05 for OSD.
papers.relevance: A close match for GaLore-style low-rank gradient optimization under tight rank budgets.

evidence.quote: when training the 130M model at an aggressively low rank of just 16, Ori achieves a validation perplexity of 43.61, substantially outperforming GaLore (60.29) and OSD (54.05).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: The paper derives LoRA rank bounds from the finite-rank map through which frozen features expose an adapted weight. Its stationary-point result requires a generic perturbation and does not rule out spurious local minima.
papers.relevance: Addresses LoRA rank sufficiency and the connection between factor weight decay and trace-norm regularization.

evidence.quote: This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem; Proposition 4.9 gives an explicit limitation.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: Under balance and alignment assumptions, the paper derives how GD, simplified Adam, Muon, Shampoo, and a K-FAC model change singular-mode birth and decay in matrix factorization.
papers.relevance: Targets how optimizer geometry changes spectral bias and effective rank, while remaining a model-based analysis rather than an LLM result.

evidence.quote: Although the phase laws rely on balance and alignment assumptions, they identify concrete mechanisms to understand optimizer behavior.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep under label noise compares adapters with dense fine-tuning. On Qwen2.5-7B, the reported gap to dense remains positive at every measured rank across three shared seeds.
papers.relevance: Connects LoRA rank, factorization, noisy-label memorization, and generalization.

evidence.quote: G G remains positive at every measured rank and in every seed, parity included.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free research harness that retrieves broad passages, returns selected snippets, and permits later context expansion. Its controlled closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two baseline harnesses.
papers.relevance: Directly applicable to retrieval and context management in a handwritten research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines multi-source discovery, identity checks, evidence assessment, and joint paper ranking. Its historical 30-query Hit@5 comparison favors it overall, but the authors caution against a broad superiority claim.
papers.relevance: Directly informs auditable paper retrieval, ranking, and evidence provenance for the digest agent.

evidence.quote: The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: Selection is bounded by the supplied screened corpus; stronger unseen papers may exist.
Code availability and reproducibility were not verified.
The retrieved passages did not establish training memory or compute overhead for spectral weight decay or BMuon.
Monarch-Muon’s large-model systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs.
Ori’s cited memory figures concern optimizer state, not total peak GPU training memory.
